settingsAutomationRulesNotOffered: Automation rules are not available here.

settingsAutomationRunsSub: Runs from the last 30 days, newest first.
settingsAutomationRunsEmptyBody: When this rule runs, each run and what it did shows here for 30 days.
settingsAutomationTryHint: The trigger and conditions are not checked: this is what the actions would do.
settingsAutomationActionRotateHint: Choose 2 to 20 people; each new record goes to the next one.
settingsAutomationActionOnePersonHint: One person takes exactly one. Choose who stays.
settingsAutomationActionDueHelper: From 0 to 365. Leave empty for no due date.
settingsAutomationActionNotifyHint: In the app and by email, to active members only.
settingsAutomationActionGone: This action is no longer available.
settingsAutomationRuleEditorLoadFailed: Could not load the rule editor.
settingsAutomationRuleSaveToTry: Save the rule to try it on a record.
settingsAutomationRuleSaveFirst: Save first: Try uses the saved rule.

settingsAutomationRuleActionsLimit: {count, plural, other{A rule can have at most {count} actions.}}
settingsWebFormNameHelper: Internal only. The visitor never sees it
settingsWebFormsNothingToCreate: Web forms create leads or tickets, and both are switched off. An admin can switch one on in Modules settings.
settingsWebFormsLiveSilent: Live but silent. Nothing has been submitted.
settingsWebFormsSecurityNote: A published form accepts posts from anyone. It has to: the whole point is that a stranger can fill it in without an account. A hidden honeypot field, per-address and per-form rate limits, and disposable-address rejection are always on. Unpublish a form the moment you take its snippet off your site.
settingsWebFormsEmptyAdmin: A web form is a page you embed on your own site. What people fill in becomes a lead or a ticket here, with no login and no copy-pasting.
settingsWebFormsEmptyMember: Nobody has built a web form for this organization yet. An administrator can create one.
settingsWebFormsLoadError: Could not load the web forms
settingsWebFormDetailUnpublishBody: It stops accepting submissions immediately. The embed stays on your site and starts refusing people.
settingsWebFormDetailDeleteBody: The form and its submission history go for good. Leads and tickets it already created stay where they are. Any embed still on your site will stop working.
settingsWebFormDetailFieldsSub: What a visitor is asked, in the order they are asked it. An email field is required before the form can be published.
settingsWebFormDetailBehaviourSubLead: What the visitor sees after they submit, and where the lead lands.
settingsWebFormDetailBehaviourSubTicket: What the visitor sees after they submit, and where the ticket lands.
settingsWebFormDetailRedirectHelper: http or https only. The embed navigates the visitor here
settingsWebFormDetailAssignHelper: A repeat submission from the same email updates the existing lead and keeps its owner
settingsWebFormDetailRotationHint: Each new lead goes to the next member in turn. Deactivated members are skipped.
settingsWebFormDetailCapHelper: Optional. A member holding this many open leads is passed over until one is converted or closed. When everyone is passed over, the lead stays unassigned
settingsWebFormDetailDeactivatedTicketHe: Deactivated users are not assigned. New tickets from this form are left to your routing rules until you choose someone else.
settingsWebFormDetailDeactivatedLeadHelp: Deactivated users are not assigned. New leads from this form stay unassigned until you choose someone else.
settingsWebFormDetailPriorityHelper: Set by the form, never by the visitor
settingsWebFormDetailNotifyLead: Email these people on each lead
settingsWebFormDetailNotifyTicket: Email these people on each ticket
settingsWebFormDetailSpamSub: A hidden honeypot field, a per-address rate limit and a per-form one are always on and are not configurable. These are the parts you choose.
settingsWebFormDetailOriginsHelper: One per line, scheme and host only. Leave empty and the iframe embed works anywhere. The script embed needs the site listed here
settingsWebFormDetailSecretStoredHint: Stored. Leave blank to keep it
settingsWebFormDetailSecretStoredHelper: Never shown again once saved. Leaving this blank keeps what is stored
settingsWebFormDetailSecretMissingHelper: No secret stored yet. Verification fails closed, so publishing with Turnstile on and no secret would refuse every submission
settingsWebFormDetailEmbedSub: Paste one of these into your own site. Both are built by the server, because they need the API address.
settingsWebFormDetailIframeNote: Works anywhere, no origin list needed.
settingsWebFormDetailScriptWarning: This one will not work yet. Add the site origin under Spam first: the browser blocks a cross-origin POST unless we permit that origin, and this form permits none.
settingsWebFormDetailActivitySub: The last 30 days. A view is counted when the embed loads, whether or not anyone fills it in.
settingsWebFormDetailAccepting: Accepting submissions from anyone with the embed.
settingsWebFormDetailCollectingNothing: Collecting nothing until it is published.
settingsWebFormDetailFieldsEmpty: No fields yet. A form with no fields collects nothing.
settingsWebFormDetailFieldIncomplete: Incomplete. It needs a label and a target.
settingsWebFormDetailSubmissionsEmpty: Nothing submitted yet. Rejected attempts would be listed here too, so an empty list means nobody has reached the form at all.
settingsWebFormFieldLabelRequired: Give the field a label. It is what the visitor reads.
settingsWebFormFieldTargetRequired: Choose what this field writes into.
settingsWebFormFieldWritesIntoTicket: Where on the ticket or its contact this answer lands
settingsWebFormFieldWritesIntoLead: The field on the lead this answer lands in
settingsWebFormFieldLabelHelper: What the visitor sees above the box
settingsWebFormFieldPlaceholderHelper: Optional. Shown inside the empty box
settingsWebFormFieldRequiredSub: The visitor cannot submit without answering
settingsWebhooksCreatedTitle: Webhook added, copy its signing secret now
settingsWebhooksSecretOnce: This is the only time the signing secret is shown. Store it where your receiver can read it; rotate it if it is lost.
settingsWebhooksMemberBody: Webhooks send copies of this organization's records to other services, and a hook URL is often a secret of its own, so only administrators can see or change them.
settingsWebhooksAtLimit: An organization can have at most {limit} webhooks. Remove one to add another.
settingsWebhooksEmptyBody: A webhook posts to a URL whenever a {kinds} changes. Point one at Zapier, n8n, Slack or your own code.
settingsWebhooksFootnote: Every JSON delivery carries an X-BottleCRM-Signature header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp and the raw body, keyed with the webhook's secret. A failed delivery is retried five times over about eight and a half hours, and an endpoint that answers 410 Gone is paused. So is every webhook whose creator stops being an admin, is deactivated or leaves; any admin can turn it back on and then answers for it.
settingsWebhookDetailRotateBody: The current secret stops verifying at once. Update your receiver straight after.
settingsWebhookDetailRotatedTitle: Secret rotated, copy the new one now
settingsWebhookDetailDeleteBody: Removes the webhook and its delivery log.
settingsWebhookDetailTestQueued: Test queued. Pull to refresh in a few seconds.
settingsWebhookDetailAnswersNote: Turning it on, changing its URL, events or format, or rotating its secret makes you the admin who answers for it.
settingsWebhookDetailDeliveriesError: Could not load deliveries. Pull to refresh.
settingsWebhookDetailDeliveriesEmpty: Nothing sent yet. Send a test, or change a record this webhook listens for.
settingsWebhookFormErrorHttps: The URL must start with https://.
settingsWebhookFormUrlHelper: HTTPS on the standard port, reachable publicly
settingsWebhookFormDescriptionHint: e.g. Zapier: new leads to the sales sheet
settingsDealPipelinesDeleteBody: Its stages go with it. A pipeline that still holds deals cannot be deleted: move them to another pipeline first.
settingsDealPipelinesFooter: Open a pipeline to see its stages. Each stage is a column on the deals board.
settingsDealPipelineSheetsNewHint: It starts with the default stages, from Prospecting to Closed Won and Closed Lost. You can rename or remove any of them.
settingsDealPipelineSheetsKindHint: Won and lost close a deal. Reports and goals read this, not the name.
settingsDealPipelineSheetsExpectedHint: A deal here longer than this reads Past expected, and Stalled at one and a half times it. Empty: never ages.
settingsDealPipelineSheetsWarningHint: An earlier Past expected, before the expected days run out.
settingsDealPipelineDetailDeleteStageBod: Its column disappears from the board. A stage that still holds deals cannot be deleted, and neither can the last open, won or lost stage.
settingsDealPipelineDetailFooter: Stages are columns on the deals board, in this order. Won and lost stages close a deal; only open stages age.
settingsDealPipelineDetailAging: {yellow, plural, =1{{kind}. Past expected at 1 day, stalled at {red}.} other{{kind}. Past expected at {yellow} days, stalled at {red}.}}
settingsLeadPipelinesDeleteBody: It disappears from the board along with its stages. A pipeline that still holds leads cannot be deleted: move them out of its stages first.
settingsLeadPipelinesFooter: Open a pipeline to see its stages. Each stage is a lane on the lead board.
settingsLeadPipelinesEmptyAdmin: A pipeline sorts leads into stages you move them through. Tap + to create one.
settingsLeadPipelinesEmptyMember: A pipeline sorts leads into stages you move them through. An administrator sets these up.
settingsLeadPipelineDetailDeleteStageBod: Its lane disappears from the board. A stage that still holds leads cannot be deleted: move them to another stage first.
settingsLeadPipelineDetailNoStagesAdmin: No stages yet. Add one so leads can be moved into this pipeline.
settingsLeadPipelineDetailFooter: Stages are lanes on the lead board, in this order. Moving a lead into a stage can set its status and win probability.
settingsLeadPipelineFormDefaultStagesOn: New, Contacted, Qualified, Proposal, Won and Lost. You can rename or remove any of them.
settingsLeadPipelineFormDefaultStagesOff: The pipeline starts empty. Add stages before moving leads into it.
settingsLeadStageFormTypeHint: Whether leads here are still open, won or lost
settingsLeadStageFormStatusHint: Applied when a lead is moved into this stage
settingsLeadStageFormProbabilityHint: 0 to 100. Given to a lead moved in with none set.
settingsCustomFieldsTurnOffBody: It stops appearing on new records and stops accepting new values. Values already stored are kept, and you can turn it back on.
settingsCustomFieldsGapsBanner: {count, plural, =1{One required field has records with no value for it. Marking a field required only binds new saves, so older records keep the gap.} other{{count} required fields have records with no value for them. Marking a field required only binds new saves, so older records keep the gap.}}
settingsCustomFieldsMissing: {count, plural, =1{1 record has no value for this} other{{count} records have no value for this}}
settingsCustomFieldsEmptyAdmin: Add one to collect something the built-in fields do not cover, on any record type.
settingsCustomFieldsLoadFailed: Could not load the custom fields
settingsCustomFieldFormLabelHint: What the field is called on the record
settingsCustomFieldFormKeyHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. Cannot be changed later.
settingsCustomFieldFormKeyFixed: Fixed after creation. Every value already stored is filed under this key, and changing it would leave them behind.
settingsCustomFieldFormTypeFixed: Fixed after creation. Values already stored were written as this type and a new one would reinterpret them.
settingsCustomFieldFormPositionHint: Lower numbers come first on the record
settingsCustomFieldFormRequiredHint: Binds new saves only. Records saved before this keep their gap.
settingsOptionsEditorHint: Renaming an option keeps the records that already use it.
settingsModulesNotOffered: This server does not offer modules yet.
settingsModulesIntro: Switch off what this organization does not use. Nothing is deleted: switching a module back on brings everything back as it was.
settingsModulesMemberOnly: Only an organization admin can switch modules on or off.
settingsModulesNeedsComesBack: Needs {module}. It comes back when {module} is switched on.
settingsRoutingDeadWarning: {count, plural, =1{One running rule has nobody to assign to. It matches tickets and leaves them unassigned.} other{{count} running rules have nobody to assign to. They match tickets and leave them unassigned.}}
settingsRoutingNobodyStops: Nobody to assign to. Matching tickets are left unassigned, and this rule stops the ones below it from trying.
settingsRoutingNobodyFallsThrough: Nobody to assign to. Matching tickets fall through to the rules below.
settingsRoutingManyInactive: {count, plural, other{{count} of the people here are deactivated and are skipped.}}
settingsRoutingFootnote: Rules run in this order and the first match wins. Routing happens once, when a ticket is created, so changing a rule does not move tickets that already exist.
settingsRoutingEmptyAdmin: New tickets arrive unassigned until a rule picks them up.
settingsRoutingEmptyMember: New tickets arrive unassigned. An administrator sets these up.
settingsRoutingLoadError: Could not load the routing rules
settingsRoutingRuleFormNoConditions: With no conditions this rule matches every new ticket.
settingsRoutingRuleFormAllTrue: All of these have to be true.
settingsRoutingRuleFormRotationHint: Picked one at a time, in turn.
settingsRoutingRuleFormNobodyToPick: Nobody to pick yet. Invite someone from Team first.
settingsRoutingRuleFormStopOn: No rule below this one gets a turn, even if this one assigns nobody.
settingsRoutingRuleFormStopOff: A ticket this rule cannot assign falls through to the rules below.
settingsEscalationUnheardWarning: {count, plural, other{{count} breaches in the last 30 days told nobody. A policy that exists is not the same as a policy that fires.}}
settingsEscalationUnconfiguredOne: {priority} has no policy, so breaches at that priority escalate to nobody and are not counted here.
settingsEscalationUnconfiguredMany: {priorities} have no policy, so breaches at those priorities escalate to nobody and are not counted here.
settingsEscalationNextReplyLine: {next} next reply, measured in analytics only. Missing it triggers no escalation.
settingsEscalationHalfBreachesIgnored: {count} in the last 30 days, none of them acted on
settingsEscalationFootnote: First response and resolution targets are measured on business hours, so a breach counts working time only, and time spent waiting on the customer does not count at all. Editing a policy sets both the target and who hears about a breach. The next reply target escalates nothing: it is counted around the clock and reported in ticket analytics. The counts cover tickets opened in the last 30 days.
settingsEscalationEmptyAdmin: A policy decides what happens when a ticket misses its first response or its resolution target. None are set, so a breach escalates to nobody.
settingsEscalationEmptyMember: A policy decides what happens when a ticket misses its first response or its resolution target. None are set, so a breach escalates to nobody. An administrator sets these up.
settingsEscalationLoadError: Could not load the escalation policies
settingsEscalationPolicyFormHoursHelper: Business hours. Blank uses the default.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormPriorityHelp: Fixed once the policy is saved
settingsEscalationPolicyFormPriorityFixe: Priority {priority}. One policy per priority, fixed after it is created.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormNextHelper: Each reply after the first, counted around the clock. Measured in analytics only: missing it triggers no escalation. Blank uses the default.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormApplyNote: First response and resolution apply to tickets opened from now on, and to any ticket moved to this priority. Tickets already open keep the target they were given. Next response is read whenever analytics are scored, so a change rescores past replies too.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormNoTeams: No teams in this organization yet.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormTeamHint: Copied in alongside the target, on halves that notify. A team is never escalated to on its own.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormInactiveTarg: This account is no longer active. It stays set until you change it, and a breach sent here waits for somebody who cannot sign in.
settingsEscalationPolicyFormReassignHint: Reassigns the ticket. No email is sent, to them or to the team.
settingsReopenMemberBody: The reopen policy and the reply figures behind it are visible to administrators. Ask one of yours whether replies to closed tickets bring them back.
settingsReopenEnabledDetail: Off means a reply is filed on the closed ticket and nothing else happens.
settingsReopenWindowDetail: Counted from when the ticket was closed, in calendar days.
settingsReopenStatusDetail: Has to be a status that counts as open, or the ticket would close again on arrival.
settingsReopenNotifyDetail: The person the ticket was assigned to when it closed.
settingsReopenLateReplies: {count, plural, other{{count} replies landed on tickets closed more than {days} days earlier, so no ticket came back and nobody was told. Those customers are still waiting.}}
settingsReopenFootnoteOn: A reopened ticket is the same ticket, keeping its history and its number, so first response and resolution are still measured from the original open. Which addresses accept replies at all is set in inbound email.
settingsReopenFootnoteOff: Turned on, a reply inside the window would bring the same ticket back rather than open a new one, keeping its history and its number. Which addresses accept replies at all is set in inbound email.
settingsReopenLoadError: Could not load the reopen policy
settingsReopenFormEnabledOn: A reply inside the window puts the ticket back in the queue.
settingsReopenFormEnabledOff: A reply is filed on the closed ticket and nothing else happens. Nothing counts those replies either, so the missed-window figure reads zero while it is off.
settingsReopenFormWindowHelper: Calendar days from when the ticket closed, {min} to {max}
settingsReopenFormStatusHelper: Only a status that counts as open
settingsMacrosBrokenWarning: {count, plural, =1{One reply uses a placeholder that is not recognized. It goes out to the customer exactly as written.} other{{count} replies use a placeholder that is not recognized. Those go out to the customer exactly as written.}}
settingsMacrosBrokenOne: {token} is not recognized and goes out as written
settingsMacrosBrokenMany: {tokens} are not recognized and go out as written
settingsMacrosEmptyBody: Write the answer you keep typing once, then insert it into a ticket reply in two taps.
settingsMacrosLoadError: Could not load the saved replies
settingsMacroFormNoMembers: No active members to choose from
settingsMacroFormNoTags: No active tags to choose from
settingsMacroFormTitleHelper: What you will look for in the reply box
settingsMacroFormMemberNote: Saved for you alone. An administrator writes the replies the whole organization shares.
settingsMacroFormBodyHelper: Leave empty for a reply that only changes the ticket
settingsMacroFormAssignHint: Replaces whoever the ticket is assigned to
settingsMacroFormTagsHint: Added to the ticket's own tags
settingsBusinessHoursAlwaysOnBanner: Every day below reads Closed, and a four-hour target still expires four hours after the ticket arrives, weekend or not. Open at least one day to make the calendar count.
settingsBusinessHoursNoHolidays: No holidays set. Targets keep running on public holidays.
settingsBusinessHoursFootnote: A ticket that arrives after closing starts its clock when the week next opens, so the hours in between do not spend a target. Service analytics is measured on this calendar too. A holiday is a full day off in this timezone, which is separate from the organization timezone.
settingsBusinessHoursLoadError: Could not load the business hours
settingsBusinessHoursFormAlwaysOn: With no day open, targets run around the clock. The engine drops a calendar that never opens rather than treating it as permanently shut.
settingsBusinessHoursFormNameError: Give the day a name, so the list reads.
settingsBusinessHoursFormHolidayIntro: A full day off in {timezone}. Targets stop for the whole of it.
settingsApprovalRulesStranding: {count, plural, =1{One active rule can be cleared by nobody. What it gates cannot be closed by anyone.} other{{count} active rules can be cleared by nobody. What they gate cannot be closed by anyone.}}
settingsApprovalRulesNobodyFlag: This organization has admins and members. There is no manager role. With no named approvers, the first ticket this gates cannot be closed by anyone. Name approvers, or set it to admin.
settingsApprovalRulesShadowedFlag: {rule} gates exactly the same tickets and was written later. One rule gates a close, the most specific match, and the newest wins between equals, so this one never runs.
settingsApprovalRulesFootnote: A ticket is gated by one rule, the most specific that matches it. The others are fallbacks for the tickets it misses. Whoever asked for the close can never be the one who clears it, whatever a rule says.
settingsApprovalRulesEmptyAdmin: Tickets close without anyone signing off. Add a rule to gate the closes that need a second pair of eyes.
settingsApprovalRulesEmptyMember: Tickets close without anyone signing off. An administrator sets these up.
settingsApprovalRulesLoadError: Could not load the approval rules
settingsApprovalRuleFormNoTeams: No teams in this org yet.
settingsApprovalRuleFormPickedHint: Anyone picked here can clear it as well as the role above, not instead of it.
settingsApprovalRuleFormStrandsWarning: This organization has admins and members. There is no manager role, so with nobody named here the first ticket this gates cannot be closed by anyone.
settingsInboundEmailSilentOne: {address} is switched on and creates nothing. Mail keeps arriving and nothing bounces, so whoever writes there gets no ticket and no error.
settingsInboundEmailSilentMany: {count, plural, other{{count} addresses are switched on and create nothing. Mail keeps arriving and nothing bounces, so whoever writes there gets no ticket and no error.}}
settingsInboundEmailAuthTitle: How a delivery is proved genuine
settingsInboundEmailEmptyAdmin: Add one and mail sent to it opens a ticket, once it is pinned to its SNS topic.
settingsInboundEmailEmptyMember: Email does not open tickets here yet. An administrator sets these up.
settingsInboundEmailLoadError: Could not load the inbound addresses
settingsMailboxFormAddressHint: Mail to the old address stops becoming tickets.
settingsMailboxFormProviderHint: Only AWS SES is implemented. Mail to an address using one of the others becomes nothing until that integration exists.
settingsMailboxFormTopicHint: Mail is accepted only from this exact topic. Left blank, it is set by the first subscription AWS confirms from an AWS account this server allows. Clearing it stops mail until it is set again.
settingsMailboxFormAssigneeHint: Where a ticket goes after that is decided by routing, not by this.
settingsMailboxFormDeactivatedHint: Deactivated users are not assigned. New tickets from this address go to routing until you choose someone else.
settingsHelpCenterOffHint: Off means every public page answers "not found".
settingsHelpCenterSummaryLive: Public, and open to search engines.
settingsHelpCenterOpenFailed: Could not open the public page
settingsHelpCenterPublicSubtitle: Publish approved, published articles for anyone to read.
settingsHelpCenterSlugHint: 3 to 50 lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens. Required before the help center can be switched on.
settingsHelpCenterFootnote: Only articles that are both approved and published are shown, the same ones customers see in the portal. Drafts, tags, linked tickets and who wrote an article never are. Search engines can list these pages.
settingsHelpCenterLoadError: Could not load the help center
settingsAuditLogEmptyFilteredBody: No entry matches these filters. Widen the dates or clear them.
settingsAuditLogEmptyBody: Sign-ins, org switches, refused requests, webhook pauses and API token or calendar feed changes appear here as they happen.
settingsAuditLogAdminsOnlyBody: The audit log records who signed in, from where, and what was refused, so only administrators can read it.
settingsCalendarFeedRegenBody: The old URL stops working at once, and calendars subscribed to it stop updating. Subscribe again with the new one.
settingsCalendarFeedOffBody: The URL stops working and subscribed calendars stop updating. You can turn it on again later with a new URL.
settingsCalendarFeedNeverRead: No calendar app has read it yet.
settingsCalendarFeedReadAt: A calendar app read it on {when}.
settingsCalendarFeedGoogleBody: On a computer, open Google Calendar. Beside Other calendars choose +, then From URL, paste the feed URL and choose Add calendar. Google refreshes it every few hours, so changes take a while to appear.
settingsCalendarFeedOutlookBody: In Outlook on the web choose Add calendar, then Subscribe from web, paste the feed URL and choose Import.
settingsCalendarFeedAppleBody: Choose File, then New Calendar Subscription, and paste the feed URL.
settingsCalendarFeedRevealTitle: Your feed URL, copy it now
settingsCalendarFeedRevealBody: This is the only time it is shown. If you lose it, regenerate it.
settingsCalendarFeedSummaryBody: Your tasks that are New or In progress and have a due date, from 90 days ago to a year ahead, as all-day events. Each shows the title, the priority and a link to the task.
settingsCalendarFeedFootnote: The URL is the key. Anyone who has it can see the titles and priorities of your open tasks without signing in, so share it with nobody but your calendar app, and regenerate it if it leaks. It stops working on its own if you leave the organisation or your account is deactivated.
settingsCalendarFeedLoadError: Could not load your calendar feed

settingsProfileGoalsDetail: Your quota and how it is pacing
settingsProfileTimesheetDetail: Hours you have logged this week
settingsProfileEditableHint: Name and phone are editable. Email and access flags are managed by your administrator.
settingsOrgCurrencyHintInvoices: Applied to new invoices and estimates. Existing ones keep theirs.
settingsOrgCurrencyHint: The default for new records that carry an amount. Existing ones keep theirs.
settingsOrgTimeZoneHint: When a day starts here, so "due today" and "overdue" mean what your team expects.
settingsOrgCascade: Close child tickets with the parent
settingsOrgPrintedNote: These fields are printed on every invoice and estimate. Changing one changes documents from that moment on; PDFs already sent keep what they were sent with.
settingsOrgApiKeyNote: The organization API key is not here. It authenticates as the whole organization, so it is never shown on a page you can reach by browsing. For per-person programmatic access, use API tokens, which can be revoked one at a time.
settingsOrgApplyBody: This adds starter pipelines, tags, custom fields and a set of sample records. Anything already set up is left exactly as it is.
settingsOrgApplyBodyProducts: This adds starter pipelines, tags, custom fields, products and a set of sample records. Anything already set up is left exactly as it is.
settingsOrgClearBody: Permanently deletes every sample record a pack created for this organization. Your real records are never touched, and any sample record you have since attached real work to is kept. This cannot be undone.
settingsOrgPackBody: A pack adds starter pipelines, tags, custom fields and sample records for one kind of business. Applying one only fills in what this organization is missing.
settingsOrgPackBodyProducts: A pack adds starter pipelines, tags, custom fields, products and sample records for one kind of business. Applying one only fills in what this organization is missing.
settingsOrgAdminsOnly: Applying a pack or clearing sample data is limited to administrators.
settingsOrgClearHint: Removes only the records a pack created as samples. Your real records are never touched.
settingsOrgEditAdminsOnlyBody: Editing organization details is limited to administrators. Ask one of yours if a company detail, currency, or survey setting needs changing.
settingsOrgEditPrintedHint: Printed on every invoice and estimate. Changes apply from now on; documents already sent keep what they were sent with.
settingsOrgEditTimeZoneHint: When a day starts for this organization. Changing it moves what counts as due today and overdue, for everyone here.
settingsOrgEditNumbersHint: How new invoice and estimate numbers look. Numbers already issued keep theirs.
settingsOrgEditStartHint: To carry on a sequence from another system. If invoices here already go higher, numbering carries on from the highest.
settingsOrgEditExample: New invoices look like {invoice}, estimates like {estimate}.
settingsApiTokensAdminsOnlyBody: Reviewing every token in the organization is limited to administrators, because a token authenticates as its owner. Ask an admin if one needs issuing or revoking.
settingsApiTokensRevokedOrphaned: {count, plural, =1{Revoked 1 token on deactivated accounts.} other{Revoked {count} tokens on deactivated accounts.}}
settingsApiTokensOrphanText: {count, plural, =1{1 live token belongs to a deactivated account. Deactivating already stops it at login, but it is not revoked. Reactivating the account would bring it back.} other{{count} live tokens belong to a deactivated account. Deactivating already stops them at login, but they are not revoked. Reactivating the account would bring them back.}}
settingsApiTokensEmpty: No tokens have been issued in this organization.
settingsApiTokensFootnote: A token authenticates as its owner and inherits their role and organization. Issue one per integration so a single revocation stops a single thing, set an expiry, and revoke anything you cannot name a use for.
settingsMyApiTokensSafetyBody: It authenticates as your profile and inherits your role and your org, so anyone holding it can do what you can. Revoke it here the moment it is not needed. An admin can see and revoke it too.
settingsMyApiTokensEmptyBody: A token lets a script, an integration or an agent call the API as you, with your role and your org. Create one when you need it, and revoke it the moment you do not.
settingsApiTokenFormIntro: The token is created for you and authenticates as you. The value is shown once, on the next screen.
settingsApiTokenFormNameHelper: Names what breaks if you revoke it later
settingsApiTokenFormAccessHelper: Finer scopes are available through the API
settingsApiTokenFormNeverWarning: A token that never expires has to be revoked by hand to ever stop working.
settingsObjectsFormNamesRequired: Give the object a singular and a plural name.
settingsObjectsFormKeyInvalid: The key starts with a letter, uses only lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, and is 2 to 28 characters.
